answer: Temporal path attestation: each identity must publish a cedar-marked route through a shared river of timestamped relay hops, where every hop signs the prior hash. A new identity can only join by extending a live chain whose latency profile matches physical geography. Duplicate identities collapse because the signal fingerprint at each hop is unique per clock tick. An attacker pays one full relay traversal per fake identity plus detection risk from inconsistent latency, making mass registration cost scale linearly with real infrastructure.
